## Briefing

::: {.rq-lesson}
Read first: [Iteration](../r-foundations/iteration.qmd). Copy-pasting the same code for 12 variables is how mistakes get in. Four safer tools: **`across()`** (one step on many columns), a **`for` loop**, **`sapply()` / `map()`** (collect one result per item) and your own **function**.
:::

```{r}
ncd |> summarise(across(c(sbp, dbp, bmi), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

```{r}
for (v in c("sbp", "dbp")) print(mean(ncd[[v]], na.rm = TRUE))      # ncd[[v]]: the column whose NAME is stored in v
pct_above <- function(x, cut) mean(x >= cut, na.rm = TRUE) * 100     # a function returns its last expression
pct_above(ncd$sbp, 140)
```

::: {.rq-lesson}
**Pitfalls.** `ncd$v` looks for a column called "v": use `ncd[[v]]`. Forgetting `na.rm = TRUE` makes every result `NA`. Do not grow a vector with `c()` in a loop; use `sapply()` / `map()`. Coding tasks are checked without running R: your own names and either pipe style are fine.
:::
